    Reference · local-first

    Data & privacy

    Local-first by construction: one SQLite file and a folder on your disk, no telemetry, and a truthful list of the seven external sources the app talks to and exactly what crosses the wire.

    Bablytics is a single-user program that runs on your own computer. It listens on 127.0.0.1, writes everything to one folder, and has no server of its own anywhere. The only traffic it generates is the traffic the features need — market data, headlines, and, if you give it a key, the Anthropic API. This page lists all of it, because a privacy page that says “we take your privacy seriously” and stops is not one.

    The whole picture#

    What stays on your machine#

    Everything the app produces or remembers. Concretely, inside the data folder (paths per OS):

    bablytics.db
    One SQLite file, WAL mode. Tables: users and sessions (one account, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 200 000 iterations, 30-day httponly session cookie), runs, leads, grades, outcomes, evening_reviews, preopen_reviews, midday_reviews, horizon_reviews, member_journal, pyramid_scores, positions and position_reviews (your uploaded holdings and the board’s reviews of them), user_trades and user_reflections (leads you marked TAKEN, trades you logged by hand, what you wrote about them), staged_orders (the Broker queue), paper_positions and paper_equity (the League), pulse_updates and rl_reports (the Pulse), lead_triggers and bailiff_events (the Bailiff), curry_cycles, settings (schedule times, Pulse goals, Schwab app key/secret if you typed them in — masked in the UI, stored in this file).
    rl/
    The Pulse’s numpy models and their roster, evaluation split and generation log. Trained on your machine from public daily bars.
    model.joblib · model.json
    The small outcome model the Executive reads, trained from your own record once it has 25 realized outcomes.
    members/*.md
    Human-readable dossiers per board member: journal entries, grading history with realized returns, pyramid standing, calibration.
    cache/
    Short-lived downloads (analyst sweeps, disclosure dumps) so a repaint does not re-fetch.
    .env · schwab_tokens.json
    Your secrets, in files you control. The token file is written with mode 0600. Neither is ever sent anywhere but to the service it belongs to.
    logs/bablytics.log
    The desktop build’s rotating log. It records start-up, scheduler activity and errors, which includes ticker symbols; treat it as private if you share it for debugging.

    Theme, dashboard layout, chart templates, bell and voice preferences live in your browser’s localStorage (keys prefixed bablytics_), not in the database.

    What goes out, source by source#

    SourceWhenWhat leaves your machineWhat comes back
    Yahoo Finance, through the yfinance libraryEvery session and every chart: the morning scan over the S&P 500 universe, per-candidate technicals, pre-market prints, analyst sweeps, the Pulse’s live prints, the League’s marks, outcomes, Charts Pro, Positions quotesTicker symbols and date ranges. Yahoo sees which symbols you look at; it does not see your holdings’ sizesQuotes, daily and intraday bars, option chains, upgrades/downgrades
    News RSS — CNBC, MarketWatch, Yahoo Finance, CNN Business, BBC Business, BBC World, Al Jazeera, The GuardianMorning briefing, Pre-Open, Midday, the News tab (10-minute cache)A plain feed request, nothing elseHeadlines, summaries, links
    BLS · BEA · Census release feedsThe 9:15 Pre-Open Check’s econ tapeA plain feed requestRelease headlines matched against an economic-print keyword list
    Quiver QuantitativeMorning briefing, only if QUIVER_API_KEY is set (24-hour cache). Without a key the collector tries the legacy public S3 dumps, which currently answer 403, and the Watchdog degrades to “no signal”Your Quiver keyCongressional trade disclosures
    Anthropic APIOnly with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; see belowPrompt text: the persona’s system prompt and the material it gradesStructured JSON: grades, comments, memos, journal entries, rationales
    Schwab APIOnly after you connect a Schwab developer app in the Broker viewOAuth authorisation and token refreshes; account reads; the single order you click Submit on, after a confirmationBalances, positions, order status
    WikipediaOnly when you run python -m bablytics.universe refresh from a checkout. Normal operation uses a constituent list baked into the code (503 tickers, snapshot 2026-08-18)A plain page requestThe S&P 500 constituent table

    That is the complete list of hosts in the code. There is no update check, no crash reporter, no analytics, no usage ping, and no account with Bablytics itself — there is nothing to have an account with.

    What the Anthropic API sees, exactly#

    Real mode means the board is a language model. Each seat is one API call with a persona system prompt and a user prompt built from what that seat needs to read. Across a weekday that is roughly: fifteen calls for the morning briefing (thirteen graders, the Skeptic, the Executive), fifteen for the Pre-Open Check, fifteen for the Midday Check-In, fifteen for the Evening Court, one per Pulse cycle (fourteen cycles between 9:30 and 16:00), plus the weekend horizon panels and anything you trigger by hand. The prompts carry:

    • the market context (index prices, VIX, regime line, cycle read) and the day’s candidates — tickers, prices, option-flow statistics, technicals, value stats, matched headlines and congressional-disclosure summaries;
    • each member’s own recent journal lessons, pyramid rank and calibration statistics — text the app generated earlier;
    • your hand-posted Curry cycle forecasts (the Timekeeper reads them);
    • your holdings, when you press Review my holdings on the Positions view — ticker, quantity and cost basis become the candidates the board grades;
    • your book in the Pulse — the tickers, entries and P&L of leads you marked TAKEN, trades you logged by hand, and your uploaded holdings — so the single per-cycle call can write the “your book” paragraph;
    • your reflections, verbatim, in the Executive’s Evening Court prompt, once you have written one since the last court;
    • each member’s own open paper positions at the Midday Check-In (paper money, not yours).

    Nothing else: not your username, not your password, not your Schwab balances (the board never reads the broker), not the database. The model name is BABLYTICS_MODEL (default claude-opus-4-8); calls are made directly from your machine to api.anthropic.com with your key, under your Anthropic account and its terms. In mock mode none of this leaves the machine, because no call is made.

    Network posture#

    • The server binds 127.0.0.1. Other machines on your network cannot reach it unless you change BABLYTICS_HOST — and if you do, remember the whole app sits behind a single password.
    • Outbound connections carry timeouts and degrade per source: a dead feed yields an empty list with a note, never a crash. The Guide itself (this documentation) loads three typefaces (Literata, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono) from Google Fonts when you are online; the app’s own dashboard loads no external fonts, scripts or images.
    • The desktop app’s macOS bundle allows arbitrary loads because some market-data feeds are plain http; the app still makes only the connections listed above.

    PDF exports#

    The morning briefing, the Evening Court and the horizon reports export as print-style PDFs. Every export asks for a password (at least 4 characters) and encrypts the file with it — AES-256 when the cryptography package is installed, pypdf’s RC4 otherwise. The dialog says what that buys, and so will this page: encryption deters casual forwarding; anyone with the password opens it. The PDF is streamed to your browser as a download (bablytics-briefing-<date>.pdf, bablytics-evening-court-<date>.pdf, …); the app keeps no copy of the rendered file.

    Backups, moves and resets#

    1. Back up: quit the app, copy the whole data folder somewhere safe. That is a complete backup — account, record, journals, models, secrets. If you must copy while it is running, include bablytics.db-wal and bablytics.db-shm with the database.
    2. Move to a new machine: install the app there, copy the folder into the new machine’s data location (or point BABLYTICS_DATA_DIR at wherever you put it), start. Your password is the one you set before; the record continues.
    3. Reset: rename or delete the data folder; the next start creates a fresh one and asks you to create an account again. Deleting only bablytics.db resets the record but keeps the trained Pulse models.
    4. Forgot the password? There is no reset flow, by design — nobody else holds a copy. The only way back in is a fresh data folder, which is why the password is worth writing down.

    Uninstalling the app on any OS leaves the data folder in place; see Uninstalling.

    Third parties, briefly#

    Yahoo Finance, the news publishers, the statistical agencies, Quiver, Anthropic and Schwab each have their own terms and privacy policies; the app is a client of theirs on your behalf and can only be as private as they are about the requests they receive. The two that can learn something specific about you are Anthropic (the prompt contents above) and Schwab (your account — but only if you connect it). Both are opt-in, both are off until you add a key or complete an OAuth flow, and both stop the moment you remove the key or the token file.
